features.name: JVM wildcards from declaration-site variance
features.scope: Emit supported contextual wildcard signatures while retaining Kotlin declaration metadata and erasure.
restrictions: Newly supported: independent method type parameters in supported ordinary generic source classes and abstract generic source interfaces; interface generic-call registration, method substitution/erasure and exact callable JVM/Kotlin metadata are checked. Ordinary nongeneric class/object generic methods already existed and are regression evidence, not a new feature count.

Contextual declaration-variance callable signatures cover final/open/type-parameter arguments, nested final variant classifiers, invariant nesting, projections, input/output/function-type modes, arrays, class constructors and interface/class/object members. Private backing-field generic signatures are not parity claims; projected exposed JVM fields and variant classifier bounds/nested supertypes remain explicit boundaries.

Independent single reference upper bounds; method shadowing, recursive/dependent/multiple bounds, generic overrides/defaults/inline/suspend/varargs, generic interface bodies and lambdas in generic members remain explicit boundaries. Existing generic classifier nested/data restrictions remain.

Fixed Java caller compiled against official output is reused with -Xverify:all. All four official/candidate Kotlin provider/consumer pairs execute. AndroidBible files are relevance evidence only; this report claims no new unchanged app-file or full-app coverage.

features.name: Checked exceptions on JVM methods
features.scope: Validate canonical Throws annotations and emit checked exception declarations for supported functions and methods, including interface methods.
restrictions: Canonical Throws for supported top-level, class, object, companion, interface abstract/default/override methods and public primary constructors; source/import aliases and real accessible Throwable subclasses. Supported function/constructor defaults preserve Exceptions on synthetic helpers and overloads. Throws suspend functions and secondary-constructor annotations retain explicit boundaries. Inheriting a Throws-bearing interface default requires an explicit override; generated inherited wrappers otherwise lose the Exceptions contract, so class/object/subinterface inheritance is rejected explicitly.

Canonical Synchronized on supported concrete static/instance methods and supported accessor use sites uses JVM ACC_SYNCHRONIZED. Interface/abstract members and invalid placements reject; suspend and value-class members reject as invalid; inline and default-argument combinations retain explicit unsupported boundaries.

Java caller is compiled once against official output and reused unchanged with -Xverify:all for both providers. Kotlin consumers compile against each provider separately. Signatures are compared for selected public declarations; existing unrelated interface DefaultImpls compatibility helpers are outside exact class-shape equivalence.
No new count for existing Utf8Decoder object Throws support, full Android application compatibility, or performance claim.

features.name: Reified reference array allocation
features.scope: Allocate JVM reference arrays with the substituted runtime component type in supported compiled inline bodies.
restrictions: Unit-returning expressions, nullable Unit and arrays with nullable Unit components in templates, and direct reified Unit array allocation remain explicitly unsupported; Unit singleton references are supported.

Reified nested array marker encodings beyond a single substituted parameter and existing parameterized generic/function classifier boundaries remain unsupported; direct concrete array components are tested.
Inline exception tables, generated nested allocations, context-sensitive invokespecial and array-owner method references retain explicit rejection boundaries.
Root Object references and inherited field resolution are prerequisite correctness repairs, not counted features.
No full Android build or performance claim.

features.name: Custom increment and decrement
features.scope: Resolve supported inc and dec operators, write results back to the target and preserve prefix or postfix values within documented boundaries.
restrictions: Prefix updates of property/custom-index targets are explicitly rejected because the pinned compiler rereads the getter after setting, contrary to the specification expansion; see the recorded oracle discrepancy.
Nullable update receivers and safe-call update/compound targets remain unsupported.
Parameterized inc/dec declarations, including defaulted or vararg parameters, are explicitly unsupported; pinned Kotlin accepts some such declarations.
Index expressions keep their standalone inferred types; literal indices requiring contextual narrowing are rejected in agreement with pinned Kotlin.
The existing ordinary overload-resolution, generic, inline and primitive compound-operator boundaries apply.
Android and full-application compatibility remain unassessed.
